The '''Istituto per le Applicazioni del Calcolo Mauro Picone''' ({{langx|en|Institute for applied mathematics "Mauro Picone"}}), abbreviated '''IAC''', is an [[applied mathematics]] [[institute]], part of the [[Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche]]. It was founded in 1927 as a private research institute by [[Mauro Picone]],<ref name="G.and.F" /> and as such it is considered the first applied and computational mathematics institute of such kind ever founded.<ref>{{harv|Fichera|1995|pp=10–11}}, {{harv|Fichera|1999|p=297}}, {{harv|Benzi|2005|loc=p. 3 of the preprint version}} and the references cited in this latter one.</ref>

==Historical notes==
The IAC was founded 1927 by Mauro Picone,<ref name="G.and.F" /> while working at the [[University of Naples Federico II]] and at the [[Istituto Universitario Navale]] as professor of [[infinitesimal calculus]].<ref>See {{harv|Ghizzetti|1986|p=111}}, {{harv|De Angelis|Sbordone|1999|p=7}}, {{harv|Fichera|1995|pp=10–11}}, {{harv|Fichera|1999|p=297}}, {{harvtxt|Ghizzetti|1986|p=111}} states explicitly his professorship, while {{harvtxt|De Angelis|Sbordone|1999|p=7}} describes briefly his involvement in teaching at the Istituto Universitario Navale.</ref> [[Luigi Amoroso]] also contributed to the founding of the institute, by providing to his former ''[[Scuola Normale Superiore|Normale]]'' schoolfellow Picone the funding for the creation of the Institute by means of the [[Banco di Napoli]].<ref>See {{Harvtxt|Fichera|1950|p=1}}, {{Harvtxt|Fichera|1986|p=81}}, {{Harvtxt|Fichera|1999|p=307}} and {{Harvtxt|Benzi|2005|loc=p. 3 of the preprint version}}.</ref>
It was only in 1932, when Picone moved from the University of Naples to the [[Sapienza University of Rome]], that the Institute became part of the Italian National Research Council.<ref>See for example {{harv|Ghizzetti|1986|p=111}}, {{harv|De Angelis|Sbordone|1999|p=7}}, {{Harvtxt|Fichera|1986|p=81}}, {{Harv|Fichera|1999|p=307}}, {{Harv|Benzi|2005|loc=p. 3 of the preprint version}}, {{Harv|Benzi|Toscano|2014|p=114}}: however many other published biographical and/or research achievements surveys on Mauro Picone cite this fact.</ref>

"''Mauro Picone and the Istituto Nazionale per le Applicazioni del Calcolo''" is a brief historical survey of Picone's role in the founding of the Istituto Nazionale per le Applicazioni del Calcolo: the Author is one of his pupils, former workers and then director of the institute. It was presented at the ''International congress in occasion of the celebration of the centenary of birth of Mauro Picone and Leonida Tonelli'' (held in [[Rome]] on May 6–9, 1985): an English translation of the title of the conference is:-''The work of Leonida Tonelli and his influence on scientific thinking in this century''.
